To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the association among multiple risk alleles in genes encoding for T cell receptor signalling molecules with seroposivity may play an important part in distinct clinical phenotypic features of rheumatoid arthritis (RA).
a combination of IRF5 (T/C; rs10488631) and CD28 (C/T; rs1980422) polymorphisms is associated with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in a case control study.
the risk variants of CD28 and IRF5 genes are common determinants for RA seropositivity and that positivity of RF alone is associated with the CTL4 risk variant in a heterozygous state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of a complex system in which the genetic architecture of RA is considered.
the analysis of the genetic architecture of RA using multiparametric statistical approaches.
the identification of genetic risk factors and their interaction in RA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk alleles of CD28 and IRF5 genes are the most important determinants of seropositivity, while the risk allele of CTLA4 gene is associated with RF positivity.
the combination of the risk alleles in IRF5 and CTLA4 and CD28 genes together with positivity for RF may be considered as a strong indicator of seropositive RA.
the genetic architecture of RA is complex and that the disease is caused by the interplay of many genes, environmental factors, and the immune response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of CD28 ( rs1980422 ) and IRF5 polymorphisms is associated with seropositive Rheumatoid Arhtritis.
the risk alleles in IRF5 and CTLA4 genes are associated with seronegativity, while the risk variants of CD28 and AFF3 genes are associated with the presence of RF and ACPA, respectively.
the combination of the risk variants in IRF5 and the risk variants of CD28 gene are associated with seropositive RA.
The main takeaway from our work is that

genetic risk factors of RA may be involved in distinct disease phenotypes, and that a combination of risk alleles in IRF5 and CTLA4 may be important in seropositivity, and the combination of risk alleles of AFF3 with positivity for ACPA may be related to more severe RA.
the combination of genetic variants in CD28 and IRF5 genes is associated with seroposivity in RA, and that this combination may be a potential marker of disease severity in RA patients.
genetic architecture of RA can be better described with the use of multiparametric methods.
